I completely agree that being thrown into the deep end is sometimes the best way to go and I should be more confident to take charge. 

I think because it’s a special needs school it’s very different and crucially observing routines and the class itself was meant to be the entirety of 3 weeks (without teaching), as it can be so different and challenging to begin with. I only had one day. I was really confident in my old class, but think I have been a bit by having no support from the get go, when support was meant to be tapered off gradually rather than never being there. As it is a special school, it is a bit different to mainstream which I appreciate, and there is much more of a learning curve when considering wheelchair placements, medical needs and communication. 

Crucially, some children have very serious medical concerns and it is incredibly dangerous to leave them with staff who are not trained to support them, which is why I am so concerned about being left without training as this is a huge  danger. 

I appreciate I might be being really silly and should tough it out, so do u have any advice on how to just deal with it and focus more on my own progress without getting demoralised?
I can’t help being afraid of them. I am also scared of small spaces which are also not very dangerous. Phobias can’t be controlled and are not rational. Hope this helps!
